title: AI Visibility Audit for Multi Location Brands: How to Check Every Market and What to Fix First
seoTitle: AI Visibility Audit for Multi Location Brands
seoDescription: How to audit what ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews say about each location or market, and which fixes to make first.
excerpt: An AI visibility audit is a fixed set of real customer questions, asked market by market, with every answer checked against what is true.

author: The SocialDM Insights Team
bodyHtml:
To audit what AI assistants say about a multi location brand, write the questions customers in each market actually ask, run them in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and record whether each location is named and whether the details are right. Fix wrong facts first, then anything that stops these tools reading your pages, then the markets where competitors are named and you are not.

I treat this as an audit in the plain sense: a fixed set of questions, a dated record of the answers, and findings ranked by what they cost you. Done that way, it can be repeated and compared, which a handful of screenshots in a slide deck cannot.

What should an AI visibility audit measure?

Three things for each location: whether you are named for questions that do not include your brand, whether the facts stated about you are accurate, and which sources the answer relies on. Being mentioned with the wrong hours is not a win.

I record each answer in a sheet with one row per question, market and tool:

ColumnWhat to record
QuestionThe exact wording asked
MarketThe city or trade area, and the location setting used
Tool and dateWhich assistant, and when it was asked
NamedYes or no, and where in the answer
AccuracyEach stated fact checked against your own records
SourcesThe links or sites the answer cited
CompetitorsWho else was named

Which questions should you ask in each market?

Ask what a customer would ask before they know your name, phrased the way they would phrase it, plus a smaller set that names your brand so you can check facts. Keep the wording identical across markets so the results compare.

For a brand with clinics, branches, stores or apartment communities, that usually means three groups. Category questions with a place, such as the best option for a service near a neighborhood. Comparison questions that put you next to a named competitor in a city. Fact questions about one location, such as Sunday hours, parking or pet rules. Twenty to forty questions per market is a workable start. In my experience answers can change between runs and between users, so ask each question more than once and treat any single answer as a sample, not a verdict.

How do you check Google AI Overviews?

Search each question from the market itself or with the location set, note whether an AI Overview appears at all, and record the links it cites. Many searches will not show one, and that is a finding too.

Google's guide to AI features says AI Overviews appear only when its systems judge them additive to classic results, and that a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet to be a supporting link, with no additional technical requirements. So for Google, the audit question is mostly an SEO question: are your location pages indexed, and do they plainly answer what was asked?

Why might an AI assistant leave a location out?

The usual causes are that the tool cannot read your pages, that your pages do not state the answer, or that other sources describe your competitors more clearly. Check access before you rewrite anything.

Each assistant uses its own crawler. OpenAI's crawler documentation says sites that block OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though they can still appear as navigational links. Perplexity's crawler documentation says PerplexityBot is used to surface and link websites in its search results, recommends allowing it in robots.txt, and publishes IP ranges for firewall rules. Security settings at the firewall or CDN can block a crawler even when robots.txt allows it, so ask your web team to confirm what actually gets through.

What should you fix first?

Fix wrong facts before anything else, because an assistant stating the wrong hours or describing a closed location as open costs you more than silence. Then fix access, then missing answers, then the sources that shape weak markets.

  1. Wrong facts. Find and correct the source, usually the Business Profile, the location page or a directory listing that disagrees with both. Google's AI Overviews help page says AI Overviews can make mistakes and explains how to report a bad one. Report it, but fix the underlying page too.
  2. Blocked or unindexed pages. Confirm the crawlers you care about are allowed and that every location page is indexed.
  3. Missing answers. If customers ask about parking, price ranges or hours and the location page does not say, add it in plain text, not inside an image or a PDF.
  4. Weak markets. Where competitors are named and you are not, look at which sources were cited and whether your location appears in them accurately.
  5. Everything else. Tone, ordering and how you are described come last.

The order matters because the first three are within your control and usually quick. The fourth takes longer and depends on sites you do not own.

How should results be reported across markets?

Report each market side by side, with dates, against the baseline from your first round. A portfolio average can hide the one city where nearly every answer names a competitor.

Keep the question set fixed between rounds so changes reflect the market rather than new wording, and list what you fixed in between so a reader can connect actions to movement. I would not tie a single round of AI answers to revenue, and I would be wary of anyone who does. Our enterprise page explains how we report search and AI visibility by market. For apartment portfolios, our post on why a community can rank on Google but miss ChatGPT covers the same gap at the property level.

Questions we hear

Which AI tools should a multi location audit include?

Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity are a sensible starting set. Whatever you pick, keep the same tools and the same questions each round so results compare.

How many questions should we ask per market?

Twenty to forty is a workable start: mostly questions without your brand name, plus a few that name a location to check facts. Ask each one more than once, because answers can change between runs.

Can we get an AI tool to correct wrong information about a location?

Google lets you report a bad AI Overview, and it is worth doing. The more lasting fix is correcting the source the answer drew on, such as your profile, your location page or a directory listing.

Does blocking AI crawlers affect visibility?

It can. OpenAI says sites that block OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, and Perplexity recommends allowing PerplexityBot if you want to appear in its results.

How often should we repeat the audit?

Quarterly suits most brands, with an extra round after a major change such as new locations, closures or a rebrand.

takeaways: An AI visibility audit asks the same real customer questions in every market and records whether each location is named and whether the facts are right.
Google says a page must be indexed and eligible for a snippet to be a supporting link in AI Overviews, so location page SEO is the starting point.
OpenAI says sites that block OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, so check crawler access before rewriting content.
Fix wrong facts first, then blocked or unindexed pages, then missing answers, then the outside sources that shape weak markets.
